response: The internet traces its roots to 1960s US Defense-funded research, with the ARPANET sending its first message in 1969 and adopting the foundational TCP/IP protocols in 1983. Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989, and the 1993 Mosaic browser popularized it, fueling the dot-com boom and subsequent 2001 crash, from which survivors like Amazon and Google became some of history's most valuable companies. The mid-2000s rise of social media, the 2007 iPhone-driven mobile internet explosion, and cloud computing have since made the web ubiquitous, connecting over 5 billion people today and underpinning nearly every aspect of modern life.
